title: iQOO Z11 Lite Brings 6,500mAh Battery and AI Tools to India's Sub-Rs 20,000 5G Segment
excerpt: The student-focused smartphone launches on July 24 with a MediaTek Dimensity 6300 chip, 44W charging and AI productivity features, available exclusively through Amazon and iQOO's e-store.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • iQOO Z11 Lite 5G launches in India on July 24, priced under Rs 20,000.
  • Features a 6,500mAh battery with 44W FlashCharge and reverse charging capabilities.
  • Equipped with MediaTek Dimensity 6300 chip and up to 6GB RAM.
  • Includes AI tools for productivity, such as live transcription and document summarization.
  • Offers IP65 water resistance and military-grade durability for everyday use.
  • iQOO Z11 Lite 5G launches in India on July 24 at under Rs 20,000, available on Amazon and iQOO's e-store.
  • Powered by MediaTek Dimensity 6300 with a 6,500mAh battery supporting 44W FlashCharge, reverse wired charging and bypass charging.
  • Ships with OriginOS 6 based on Android 16, with AI Captions for live transcription and AI Creation for text summarisation.
  • Features IP65 dust and water resistance, military-grade durability certification and a Dynamic Light LED notification ring.

iQOO will launch the Z11 Lite 5G in India on July 24, positioning it as a feature-dense budget contender priced under Rs 20,000. The announcement, made by iQOO India CEO Nipun Marya, marks the brand's latest push into the sub-Rs 20,000 segment with a phone aimed squarely at students and young professionals.

A dedicated Amazon microsite is already live, confirming online availability through the e-commerce platform alongside iQOO's own e-store and retail partners.

What's Under the Hood

The Z11 Lite runs on MediaTek's Dimensity 6300 chipset — a 6nm octa-core processor that has become the standard silicon for budget 5G phones in India. iQOO claims the handset scored over 579,000 on AnTuTu, a respectable benchmark figure for its price tier. The phone pairs the chip with up to 6GB of LPDDR4X RAM and up to 256GB of UFS 2.2 storage.

The 6.74-inch HD+ IPS LCD display delivers a 120Hz refresh rate and peaks at 1,200 nits brightness — a number iQOO says is the highest in its segment. The panel uses a waterdrop-style notch rather than a punch-hole cutout.

Battery capacity is a headline feature. The 6,500mAh cell supports 44W FlashCharge, and iQOO has added reverse wired charging and bypass charging — a feature typically reserved for pricier phones that lets users run directly off the charger during gaming without cycling the battery. The company also promises five-year battery health.

Camera and Build Quality

The rear camera setup includes a 50MP Sony primary sensor alongside a 2MP secondary lens, housed in a pill-shaped module with an LED flash. A 5MP front camera handles selfies and video calls. On the build side, the Z11 Lite carries an IP65 rating for dust and water resistance and holds military-grade durability and SGS 5-Star Drop Resistance certifications — durability claims that matter for a phone likely to be tossed into backpacks daily.

A distinctive design element is the Dynamic Light feature: a multi-colour LED ring positioned below the rear cameras that pulses different colours for incoming calls, messages and notifications. Two colour options will be available at launch — Solar Flame, a textured marble-white finish, and Midnight Blue.

AI Features and Software

The Z11 Lite ships with OriginOS 6 based on Android 16. iQOO is marketing the device under a "Non-Stop Intelligence" banner, bundling two AI productivity tools aimed at students. AI Creation handles document summarisation, text rewriting, translation and brainstorming. AI Captions provides live transcription and one-tap summaries during lectures, meetings and YouTube videos.

On the software update front, iQOO has committed to two years of OS upgrades and four years of security patches. The phone is manufactured at Vivo's Greater Noida facility in India.

Where It Fits in a Crowded Market

The sub-Rs 20,000 segment in India is fiercely competitive, with Realme, Samsung and Redmi all fielding Dimensity 6300-powered devices. The Z11 Lite's pitch rests on its outsized battery, AI tools and durability certifications — a combination that could appeal to cost-conscious buyers who prioritise longevity over raw performance or display resolution.

The phone will compete directly with Realme's Narzo 100x 5G, also launching this month, and Samsung's Galaxy M-series devices in the same bracket.

What to Watch

The exact launch price — and whether iQOO's "under Rs 20,000" figure reflects effective pricing after bank offers or the sticker price — will be the deciding factor. First sale details and introductory offers are expected during the July 24 launch event.
